Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

mara said the sign supplier can take the cardboard sleeve only if it is clean and dry so it will stay in the truck until the delivery driver arrives if rain starts before the panel is mounted the crew will cover the replacement with the tarp and postpone the work rather than leave wet cardboard around the brackets the tarp is folded behind the first aid kit and the bungee cords are in the side pocket of the ladder bag the crew lead has the key for the tool shed and will lock it before going back down the service road

when i send the scan and work sheet leon can file them with the spring inspection notes but the replacement date should stay blank until the crew finishes the work the old panel may be returned to the rack for the parks office to review and no one has decided whether it will be repaired or recycled the route map and the photo will make it possible to check the lettering later if a visitor reports that the mileage looks different the north gate is expected to be busy during the weekend bird walk so the work area needs to be clear before friday afternoon i have packed the small bag of extra washers with the work sheet and will make sure the signed page stays flat during the walk back to the truck", "output": "I am at the north gate of Alder Creek Trail on Tuesday morning with the replacement sign leaning against the inside wall of the tool shed. The old sign is still attached to the post, but the lower right corner has split around two of the screws, and the lettering for the creek crossing is hard to read from the path. The new panel is cedar colored with dark green letters, and it has the same route number seven and the same mileage to the picnic shelter as the old one. I checked those details against the paper map before anyone unloaded the ladder.

Mara from the parks office brought the sign out in a flat cardboard sleeve and set it on two sawhorses so the edges would not drag across the gravel. She said the sleeve should go back in the maintenance truck because the supplier may collect it on the next delivery. The metal brackets are in a separate bag, and one bag has four bolts, washers, and lock nuts, while the small bag has two extra washers. I am forwarding the signed work sheet and the updated map to Leon at the district desk this afternoon. The work sheet has the gate location, the post number, and the name of the crew lead on the first page.

The weather has stayed dry since Monday, but the forecast calls for showers after three, and the north path gets slick when the leaves are wet. We are planning to remove the damaged panel before lunch and keep the post in place because it is straight and does not move when pushed. If the post loosens while the old panel is off, we will stop and call the parks office before mounting anything new. The replacement cannot be installed safely on a leaning post, and there is no spare post in the truck today.

1. Bring the step ladder from the storage bay and put the orange cone on the trail side of the work area.
2. Photograph the old sign in place, including the cracked corner and the post number.
3. Loosen the top screws first while someone supports the lower edge.
4. Put the old panel in the marked return rack rather than leaving it beside the path.
5. Compare the new lettering and route number with the map before tightening the brackets.
6. Record the time the crew leaves the gate in the work sheet. The crew lead asked us not to write a guessed time. If the radio clock and phone clock differ, use the radio clock and note that choice in the margin.

At the trail junction, a family stopped while we were checking the route line, and the father asked whether the picnic shelter was still open. The shelter is open, but the drinking fountain is shut off for seasonal maintenance, and the nearest working fountain is by the lower parking lot. Mara told him the creek bridge has a narrow walking surface and said, “Please keep children beside you while you cross the bridge.” He thanked her and continued toward the shelter. The junction map has a small blue dot for the fountain and a brown square for the shelter, and both marks are still easy to see on the paper copy.

Leon wants the signed work sheet sent with a scan of the old sign photograph because the district file does not include a close view of the damaged corner. The crew lead has already written the post number in the top margin, and Mara has checked the replacement panel against the route map. The map copy for the file is dated April eighth and shows the short connector to the lower parking lot in dotted blue. The public map at the gate is older and does not show that connector, so we should not use it to check the fountain directions. I will label the scan “north gate sign” and include the date on the file name.

Mara said the sign supplier can take the cardboard sleeve only if it is clean and dry, so it will stay in the truck until the delivery driver arrives. If rain starts before the panel is mounted, the crew will cover the replacement with the tarp and postpone the work rather than leave wet cardboard around the brackets. The tarp is folded behind the first aid kit, and the bungee cords are in the side pocket of the ladder bag. The crew lead has the key for the tool shed and will lock it before going back down the service road.

After the site check, we also need to leave the temporary notice at the north gate so hikers know that the crew may be working near the post. The notice says the trail remains open and asks visitors to pass slowly while the ladder is set up. It does not close the creek crossing, and it does not direct people onto the service road. Mara has two clips for the notice, but one clip is bent and should not be used. The other clip fits the wooden rail beside the map case without covering the route number.

When I send the scan and work sheet, Leon can file them with the spring inspection notes, but the replacement date should stay blank until the crew finishes the work. The old panel may be returned to the rack for the parks office to review, and no one has decided whether it will be repaired or recycled. The route map and the photo will make it possible to check the lettering later if a visitor reports that the mileage looks different. The north gate is expected to be busy during the weekend bird walk, so the work area needs to be clear before Friday afternoon. I have packed the small bag of extra washers with the work sheet and will make sure the signed page stays flat during the walk back to the truck."}]
